summary.headline: VA Tech Wabag Q2 FY27 revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore and PAT over INR 100 crore; order book hit a record INR 20,207 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations grew 20% YoY, with PAT up 23% and EBITDA of INR 145 crore at about 14.5% margin. H1 consolidated revenue rose 20.3% to INR 1,887 crore, EBITDA rose about 21% to INR 261 crore, and PAT rose almost 30% to INR 195 crore. Order book closed H1 at a record INR 20,207 crore on H1 order intake of over INR 5,200 crore, and net cash crossed INR 1,000 crore. Management flagged Middle East shipping and commodity pressures but said these have not yet hit execution timelines or margins.

financial_highlights.change: up almost 30% YoY; margin vs 9.6% last year

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,587 crore / INR 227 crore / INR 169 crore
financial_highlights.change: revenue up 19%, EBITDA up 20%, PAT up almost 29%
vs INR 950 crore at end FY26
H1 order intake over INR 5,200 crore; over 4x annual revenue

segments.name: Geography (H1 revenue)
segments.commentary: International markets contributed 54% of H1 revenue and India 46%. Middle East is about 60-70% of the international order mix.

segments.name: Business (H1 revenue)
segments.commentary: EPC accounted for 82% and O&M for 18% of H1 revenue. Management wants O&M at 20% of revenue over time.

segments.name: Order book mix
segments.commentary: Chennai is more than 10% of the total book (about 15-20% of EPC). Overall mix is roughly 55% India and 45% international per the call exchange.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term targets reiterated: revenue CAGR 15%-20%, EBITDA margin 13%-15%, ROCE above 20%, ROE above 15%, O&M at 20% of revenue, and sustained positive net cash.
EBITDA margin guidance of 13%-15% is multi-annual and includes pass-through of commodity inflation under contract formulas; management asked investors to judge margins annually, not quarterly.
Al Haer sewage treatment plant commissioning targeted for Q4 FY27; Nepal liquid-stream commissioning expected by end of FY27; Ras Tanura hydro testing targeted by November end.
Wriddhi 2.0 five-year strategy to be unveiled at the annual investor meet in May 2027.
Management expects the next 12-18 months to be a bumper order intake period, aiming to become preferred bidder on a larger pipeline in the next one or two quarters.

Employee expenses expected to stabilise; Wage Code impact remains. Management aims for positive operating cash flow of at least INR 500 crore on a pre-tax basis for FY27 (endeavour, per analyst question).
capex_capacity: Kuwait MIGD project: 60 MIGD (about 272 million litres per day) SWRO desalination with HEISCO, plus five-year O&M after EPC; contract of about USD 400 million with JV partner.
Reliance Jamnagar desalination plant of about 201 MLD, expandable to about 302 MLD, plus a remineralisation plant of about 72 MLD.
Chennai Metro Perur 400 MLD desal: about 90% concreting done, roughly 1 lakh cubic metres poured, 7 million safe man-hours; mechanical erection progressing, completion expected in the coming year.
Al Haer civil works more than 80-85% complete; mechanical erection started; final mechanical completion stage.
Yanbu desal: basic engineering substantially ready; long-lead equipment procurement started before formal commencement.
Bangladesh (World Bank funded): engineering nearly complete, ordering 90% done, 30-40% material dispatched and civil works 30-40%; about six months delay expected and to be absorbed.
Indosol Solar (Andhra Pradesh): 900 of 1,000 acres secured; 1 GW phase nearly ready for commissioning; multi-GW project waits for the balance land, expected within a quarter or few months.
demand_pricing: Order intake of over INR 5,200 crore in H1, with Kuwait and Reliance as the two mega wins; Reliance also gave a repeat medium order for an effluent treatment plant in Jamnagar in September.

Other H1 wins: Ajman wastewater treatment (UAE), Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (two projects), Delhi Jal Board medium order, Vienna waterworks expansion (Austria), and an O&M contract with Adani.
Middle East new-project awards are slower as governments reassess investment; Saudi is cautious, though some preferred-bidder projects are expected to move in about a quarter.
Management said EP share should average 20-30% of orders; H1 intake was EP-heavy (Kuwait and Reliance about 80% of intake per the CFO's statement).

Pricing and risk: Indian contracts carry escalation formulas; international contracts are hedged soon after order award. Projects are chosen for sovereign guarantees, multilateral funding (World Bank, JICA, ADB, KfW) or letters of credit.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Middle East execution headwinds and margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity prices and regional disruption are hitting supply chains, but execution and margins have not been materially affected since most work is now at site. Sea shipment delays are the main issue; air freight is used for critical parts, and a strategy is needed if delays persist for 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will Middle East pipeline conversion slow in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly, as governments are waiting on investment strategies. Kuwait (about USD 400 million with JV partner) and Ajman have moved, and Saudi preferred-bidder projects are expected to start within about a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify the bid pipeline for the next 12-18 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described peak bidding activity with large-ticket inquiries across India, GCC, Europe and Africa, and expects a bumper order intake in the next 12-18 months, aiming for preferred-bidder status in the next one or two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 gross margin one-off, and is 13%-15% EBITDA still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there is no one-off; the improvement reflects project mix and execution quality. Margins have stayed within 13%-15% for five to six years, and commodity inflation is covered by contract pass-throughs.

qa_highlights.question: Why are employee and other expenses high in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said employee cost (INR 99 crore) reflects increments, performance pay and the Wage Code impact, with no one-offs; other expenses (INR 160 crore) are regular provisions that will normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Are there sunrise-sector opportunities (semiconductor, data centres, green hydrogen, solar)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said these are of interest with a separate vertical. Order sizes are smaller and modular, with 12-15 month gestation, and data-centre water cooling is a focus. Inquiries are coming from Google, Adani and Reliance.

risks_watch: Middle East shipping delays and commodity price pressure could hit the supply chain if the disruption lasts beyond 3-6 months.
Slower new Middle East awards (especially Saudi) could weigh on order intake in H2 FY27.
Indosol Solar's land acquisition (100 of 1,000 acres still pending) may delay the multi-GW project.
Bangladesh World Bank-funded project may see about six months of delay.
Al Haer commissioning (Q4 FY27) and Ras Tanura hydro testing are near-term milestones to track.
Order book restatement from forex movements is excluded from order intake; the implied book differs from simple roll-forward (flagged by an analyst, not fully resolved).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, order book and bidding pipeline. Cautious on the Middle East, where management acknowledged slower new awards and shipping issues but said execution is intact.
key_quotes: The first time ever, our order book has surpassed INR 20,000 crores, while our net cash position has surpassed INR 1,000 crores, achieving record levels in both parameters.
There is no one-off. It is a structural improvement that is there.
We don't take projects which does not give us a payment security.

growth.why: Medium-term revenue CAGR of 15-20% held, backed by a record INR 20,207 crore order book (over 4x annual revenue) and H1 revenue up 20.3%, with named plants (Kuwait 60 MIGD, Reliance 201 MLD, Chennai 400 MLD, Al Haer) under construction or commissioning; the 17.5% figure is the midpoint of the CAGR range, not a single-year guide.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin about 14.5% and H1 about 14% sit inside the 13%-15% medium-term band, but management asked investors to judge margins annually and flagged Middle East shipping and commodity pressure, with contract pass-throughs covering inflation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Al Haer sewage plant commissioning targeted Q4 FY27 (civil 80-85% complete), Nepal liquid stream by end FY27, Chennai Metro 400 MLD completion in the coming year, and Indosol 1 GW phase nearly ready, though the multi-GW phase waits on 100 of 1,000 acres still pending.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex or new capacity investment by the company itself was not discussed; the brief covers only project-level capacity for clients.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was reiterated, not raised; management described its medium-term targets as unchanged and margins as steady within the 13%-15% band.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Bangladesh World Bank project faces about six months of delay, Indosol multi-GW phase awaits land, and Middle East shipping delays could hit execution if they persist beyond 3-6 months, though management says timelines and margins are not yet affected.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Sunrise-sector verticals (data-centre water cooling, semiconductor, green hydrogen, solar) are being pursued in a separate vertical with 12-15 month gestation and inquiries from Google, Adani and Reliance, but no launch date or size was given; Wriddhi 2.0 strategy comes May 2027.

rows.label: Preferred-bidder wins on larger pipeline
rows.why: Management aims to become preferred bidder on a larger pipeline in the next one or two quarters and expects a bumper order intake over the next 12-18 months, after H1 intake of over INR 5,200 crore; Saudi preferred-bidder projects expected to move within about a quarter.

rows.label: Middle East award slowdown
rows.why: Governments are reassessing investment and Saudi is cautious, which could slow order intake in H2 FY27 even though Kuwait (about USD 400 million) and Ajman have moved.

rows.label: Positive pre-tax operating cash flow of INR 500 crore for FY27
rows.why: Management aims for at least INR 500 crore pre-tax operating cash flow as an endeavour, against H1 consolidated operating cash flow of INR 225 crore (over 1.1x H1 PAT) and NWC days down to 101 from 104.
